lessons.title: Listening to a radio announcement
lessons.objective: Listen to a text, carry out specific tasks and answer questions about it.
lessons.course: Radio announcements give important information: who, what, where, when. We listen for key words and write short notes, not full sentences.

support.title: Radio announcement
support.text: Attention, please! The vaccination campaign against polio will take place in Mamfe from Monday 10th to Friday 14th. All children under five should be taken to the nearest health centre between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. Vaccination is free. Bring your child’s health card.

lessons.model: The adult listens to the announcement and writes notes in a table: what, where, when, who, cost.
lessons.guided: Listen to the announcement twice. Fill a table with notes. Then tell the message to someone in your own words.
lessons.exercise: How much does the vaccination cost?
lessons.remediation: Listen for one piece of information at a time.
lessons.transfer: Listen to a radio news item at home and tell your family two pieces of information.

practice.prompt: Who should be vaccinated?
Listen and write the town.
practice.listen: Attention, please! The vaccination campaign against polio will take place in Mamfe from Monday to Friday.

practice.prompt: What must parents bring?

lessons.title: Reading meaning from pictures and signs
lessons.objective: Read the meaning expressed by pictures, symbols and signs and explain them in sentences.
lessons.course: Pictures and signs give messages without many words: a red circle with a line means “not allowed”; a battery symbol shows the charge of a phone; a green arrow shows the way out. Road signs, phone icons and posters use pictures so that everyone understands quickly.
lessons.model: The adult shows a phone screen: “This envelope means a new message. This bar shows the network.”
lessons.guided: Look at six signs and symbols (no phones in class, exit, message, low battery, no smoking, hospital). Write what each means.
lessons.exercise: What does a red circle with a line across a phone mean?
lessons.remediation: Start with signs you see every day at school.
lessons.transfer: Find three signs in your town and explain them to your family.

practice.prompt: Match each symbol with its meaning.
pairs: a green arrow over a door
practice.answer: envelope: message; arrow: exit; red cross: health.

practice.prompt: Why do signs use pictures?
Draw a sign for your classroom and write its meaning.
practice.explanation: Use a picture and few words.

lessons.title: Writing a short letter with correct punctuation
lessons.objective: Write a short friendly letter using paragraphs, capital letters and punctuation correctly.
lessons.course:
A friendly letter has: the address and the date (top right), the greeting (Dear Bih,), paragraphs (news, questions), the closing (Your friend, / Yours lovingly,) and the name.
Punctuation: capital letters for names, towns, days and the start of sentences; full stops, question marks, commas after the greeting and the closing.
lessons.model: The adult writes a letter to a cousin on the board, pointing to each part and each capital letter.
lessons.guided: Write a letter of two short paragraphs to a friend in another town. Check capitals and punctuation.
lessons.remediation: Fill in a letter template first.
lessons.transfer: Write a letter to a relative and post or send it with an adult.

practice.prompt: Put the parts of the letter in order.
practice.answer: address and date, greeting, paragraphs, closing.
practice.explanation: A letter has a fixed order.

practice.prompt: Which word needs a capital letter?
practice.explanation: Days take a capital letter: Monday.

practice.prompt: Write your letter to a friend.
practice.answer: A letter with greeting, paragraphs and closing.

lessons.title: Conditional sentences: if it rains, if I had a phone
lessons.objective: Use the first and second conditional to talk about possible and imaginary situations.
lessons.course:
First conditional — a real possibility: If + present, will + verb. “If you call me, I will answer.” “If it rains, the network will be weak.”
Second conditional — an imaginary situation: If + past, would + verb. “If I had a phone, I would call my grandmother every day.” “If I were a journalist, I would interview the mayor.”
lessons.model: The adult says: “If the battery is low, I will charge the phone. If I had a computer, I would write stories.”
lessons.guided: Complete five first-conditional sentences and write three second-conditional dreams.
lessons.exercise: Complete: If you send me a message, I … (answer).
lessons.remediation: Start with the first conditional only.
lessons.transfer: Tell your family three things you would do if you had a phone.

practice.prompt: Complete with the first conditional.
practice.text: If it [[rains]], we [[will]] stay at home.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is a second conditional?
choices: If I had a radio, I would listen to the news.
If you call, I will come.
practice.answer: If I had a radio, I would listen to the news.

practice.prompt: Write: If I had a phone, I would…

lessons.title: Perimeter and area of a triangle: a road sign
lessons.objective: Calculate the perimeter of a triangle and its area using base and height.
lessons.course:
Perimeter of a triangle = side 1 + side 2 + side 3. A triangular road sign with sides of 60 cm has a perimeter of 180 cm.
Area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2. A triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm: 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20 cm². (It is half of a rectangle.)
lessons.model: The adult cuts a rectangle along its diagonal: two equal triangles, each half the area.
lessons.guided: Draw three triangles on squared paper. Measure the base and the height and calculate the area. Calculate the perimeter.
lessons.exercise: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?
lessons.remediation: Draw the rectangle around the triangle and take half.
lessons.transfer: Find triangles in signs and roofs and estimate their perimeter.

practice.prompt: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 7 cm and 8 cm. Perimeter in cm?
Base 12 m, height 4 m. Area in m²?
A triangle is … of a rectangle with the same base and height.
practice.explanation: The diagonal cuts the rectangle in two.

lessons.title: The circle: radius, diameter and circumference
lessons.objective: Identify the radius and diameter of a circle and calculate its circumference.
lessons.course:
The radius goes from the centre to the edge. The diameter crosses the circle through the centre: diameter = 2 × radius.
The circumference is the distance round the circle: C = π × diameter, with π ≈ 3.14. A satellite dish with a diameter of 2 m has a circumference of about 3.14 × 2 = 6.28 m.
lessons.model: The adult wraps a string round a tin, unrolls it and compares it with the diameter: a little more than 3 times.
lessons.guided: Measure the diameter and the circumference of three round objects with a string. Divide C by d each time.
lessons.exercise: A circle has a radius of 5 cm. What is its diameter?
lessons.remediation: Draw circles with a compass or a string and a pencil.
lessons.transfer: Measure the circumference of a bucket or a tyre at home.

practice.prompt: A circle has a diameter of 10 cm. Circumference in cm (π ≈ 3.14)?
Match each word with its meaning.
pairs: edge to edge through the centre
practice.explanation: These are parts of a circle.

practice.prompt: The diameter is … the radius.

lessons.title: Problems in several steps: phone credit and messages
lessons.objective: Solve problems that need more than one operation.
lessons.course:
To solve a problem: read it twice, find what is asked, choose the operations, calculate step by step, and check the answer makes sense.
Example: Papa buys 2 phone cards of 1 000 frs and 1 card of 500 frs. He pays with a 5 000 frs note. Step 1: 2 × 1 000 + 500 = 2 500 frs. Step 2: 5 000 − 2 500 = 2 500 frs change.
lessons.model: The adult solves the example aloud, writing each step on a separate line.
lessons.guided: Solve four problems with two or three steps about phone credit, letters and parcels.
lessons.exercise: A message costs 25 frs. Ayuk sends 12 messages and pays with 500 frs. What is his change?
lessons.remediation: Write “Step 1” and “Step 2” and solve one at a time.
lessons.transfer: Make up a two-step problem about your family’s shopping and solve it.

practice.prompt: 3 envelopes at 150 frs and 2 stamps at 300 frs. Total in francs?
A parcel costs 2 400 frs. Four friends share the cost equally and each also pays 100 frs for the bag. How much does each pay?
What do we do first in a problem?
choices: read it carefully and find what is asked
practice.answer: read it carefully and find what is asked

lessons.title: Reading and interpreting a table and a pictogram
lessons.objective: Read and interpret data in a table and a pictogram and solve problems with them.
lessons.course:
A pictogram uses a picture to stand for a number of things: one envelope = 10 letters. Half a picture = 5 letters.
To read it: count the pictures, multiply by the key, and compare rows.
lessons.model: The adult reads a pictogram of letters posted each day at the post office: Monday 4 envelopes = 40 letters.
lessons.guided: Read a pictogram of messages sent in a week. Answer five questions and draw your own pictogram.
lessons.exercise: One envelope = 10 letters. How many letters do 3½ envelopes show?
lessons.remediation: Count in tens with the envelopes.
lessons.transfer: Make a pictogram of the calls or messages your family receives in a week.

practice.prompt: Monday 40 letters, Tuesday 25, Wednesday 30. How many letters in the three days?
One picture = 10 letters. How many pictures for 60 letters?
Draw a pictogram with a key for a week of messages.
practice.answer: A pictogram with a key and seven rows.
